summary: Two clients hold the same Quote on one equity: the instrument is subscribed once, and each tick reaches both; the first client's unsubscribe sends nothing upstream and its frames stop, the other keeps getting them, and the last unsubscribe lets the instrument go.

notes: The review's coverage table asks for an exact same-mode two-client sequence (codex/WEBSOCKET_PARITY_REVIEW_1.0.7.md, Firstock row).

Both sides count holders per instrument and mode: the web server's subscription index and the adapter's reference count (_should_ws_subscribe), the desktop's registry; an extra subscribe frame would precede the unsubscribe the script waits for.

deviations.reason: Firstock's i_last_trade_time is in epoch seconds and the web sends it unchanged as ltt; feed timestamps are epoch milliseconds (docs/prompt/websockets-format.md). The desktop sends the trade time in ms.

The web's Quote sends oi 0 for an equity whose tick carries no open interest (data.get("i_open_interest", 0)); a value the broker did not send is left out, never sent as 0 (docs/api/websocket-streaming/quote.md, web openalgo#2376). The desktop's Quote leaves it out.
